texts.preamble: Munnalal vs State Of M.P. & Ors. on 16 November, 2017 1 Criminal Revision No.1527/1999 [Munna Lal Vs. State of M.P. and another] High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Principal Seat Jabalpur Single Bench: Hon. Shri Justice G.S. Ahluwalia Criminal Revision No.1527/1999 .........Applicant: Munna Lal Versus .........Respondents: State of M.P. and another Smt. Sushila Paliwal, Counsel for the applicant. Shri Manish Awasthy, Public Prosecutor for respondent/State.
texts.facts: She after going through the record, argued the matter on behalf of the applicant. Thereafter, the Food Inspector, purchased 750 M.L. of milk for a consideration of Rs.4.50 from the applicant after giving him a Munnalal vs State Of M.P. & Ors. on 16 November, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79362721/ 1 notice. The milk was equally distributed and stored in three dry and clean glass bottles and in every bottles, 20 drops of formalin were added and were sealed after affixing labels on them. One sample was sent to Public Analyst with sample of seal. The milk was found adulterated and after obtaining permission for prosecution, complaint was filed against the applicant. The applicant abjured his guilt and pleaded not guilty.
texts.arguments: It is submitted by the Counsel for the applicant that the Trial Court has not appreciated the evidence, which has come on record, in proper perspective and the incident took place in the year 1989 and therefore, a lenient view may be adopted while sentencing the applicant. The submission made by the Counsel for the applicant that since, the evidence of G.S. Gour (P.W.1) is not supported by the independent witnesses, therefore, he should not be believed as he is an interested witness. This Court in the case of Mohd. Baitulla Vs. State of M.P. reported in ILR (2011) MP 2607 has held as under : 16.
